chunks: "Whoever walks to the mosque, he does not place his feet upon anything moist or dry except that it glorifies for him down to the seven earths."
And I have presented these reports with their chains, and what was narrated regarding their meaning, in the Book of the Virtue of Mosques, their sanctity, and what has come concerning them.

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.الْأَرَضِينَ السَّابِعَةِ: the seven earths, indicating the breadth and depth of this glorification
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place of salat (prayer) and worship
key_terms.رَطْبٍ: anything moist that the walker steps upon
key_terms.يَابِسٍ: anything dry that the walker steps upon
key_terms.يُسَبِّحُ: glorifies Allah on behalf of or for the benefit of the person

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for walking to the mosque in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith speaks of the immense merit of walking to the mosque. It describes that whatever the person steps on, whether moist or dry, glorifies Allah for that person down to the seven earths, showing the spiritual reward attached to devotion and attendance at the mosque.
